title: Vara Health pilot eval scope workshop
summary: Kickoff scoping for a 4-week pilot to validate quality and economics of using Redwood for Vara Health's clinical note summarization. Discussed golden prompts, regression/golden set, hallucination and format checks, scoring rubric, workload sizing, baseline perf numbers, and next steps to run initial benchmarks and share a pilot plan and SOW.
topics: Golden prompts and golden set creation
action_items: Alex Chen: Send pilot SOW template and pricing deck (due: 2026-07-22)
Priya Nair: Prepare benchmark harness and list of initial model variants we recommend (due: 2026-07-21)
Samir Patel: Share 500 de-identified clinical notes sample and format spec (due: 2026-07-20)
Maya Gonzales: Confirm SOC2 controls required and any extra retention rules (due: 2026-07-23)
next_steps: Redwood to run dry-run benchmarks within 5 business days of receiving sample data
Align on golden set (100-200 examples) and grading rubric by July 24
Schedule 30m follow-up to review initial benchmark results week of July 27
Finalize pilot SOW and sign to start the 4-week pilot
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-18 15:30 PDT | Duration: ~52m | Attendees: Alex, Priya (Redwood) — Jordan, Samir, Maya (Vara)

[00:00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everybody — thanks for making time. Quick intros? I'll keep this tight, we want to land the pilot scope and success criteria.
[00:00:12] Jordan (Vara PM): Hi, Jordan here. We're building a clinical summarization flow for telehealth encounters. Main ask: reduce physician documentation time and improve downstream coding accuracy.
[00:00:20] Samir (Vara ML): Samir — I run the ML infra. Curious about throughput and cost tradeoffs.
[00:00:25] Maya (Vara Sec): Maya from security — I'll focus on data residency and logs.
[00:00:30] Priya (SE): Great, thanks. High-level agenda: success metrics, golden prompts/regression, hallucination checks, workload sizing, timeline. We'll propose a 4-week pilot with explicit acceptance gates.
[00:00:45] Jordan: Sounds good. On success criteria — what do you usually accept as a pass for quality?
[00:00:50] Alex: We typically use a mix: automated metrics (ROUGE-ish for structure), hallucination rate threshold, and human acceptability. For clinical summarization we've seen customers set a target of >85% clinician acceptability and hallucination under 2-3% on the golden set.
[00:01:10] Samir: The hallucination metric — is that semantic hallucination or factual contradictions specific to patient data? We need clarity.
[00:01:18] Priya: Good call. We define hallucination categories: extraneous assertions about patient history, invented meds, or dates. We'll run a detector and also human review on the golden set to label false positives.
[00:01:30] Jordan: We can get legal to scrub 500 de-id notes. Is 500 enough for initial benchmarks?
[00:01:36] Priya: For throughput and artifact checks, yes. For scoring and regression you'll want a golden set of ~100-200 high-quality examples manually annotated. The 500 bulk helps for load sizing and false-positive estimates.
[00:01:48] Alex: Side note — we'll use Redwood Hosted for the pilot unless you require a VPC. We can also run on Dedicated if predictability is critical.
[00:02:00] Maya: Likely need VPC or Private later. For pilot we can start with hosted if logs are redacted and KMS is used. What are your retention and encryption defaults?
[00:02:10] Alex: Hosted default is 30 days for debug logs; we can adjust retention and integrate with your KMS. We'll share the security playbook link after this call.
[00:02:20] Jordan: OK. Back to quality — what does a golden prompt look like for clinical summaries?
[00:02:26] Priya: Golden prompts are small templates plus a few variants. For example: "Patient encounter: [transcript]. Generate a concise HPI (history of present illness), exam summary, and 3 action items. Use present-tense and include only facts mentioned." We'll iterate with you — these prompts seed the golden set outputs.
[00:02:48] Samir: Will we be doing few-shot examples in the prompt or rely on model fine-tuning?
[00:02:52] Priya: Pilot is prompt-engineering + model selection + quantized variants. No fine-tuning initially; we want to measure out-of-the-box performance across variants (open model vX, redwood-optimized kernels). If we need fine-tune later, that's a separate engagement.
[00:03:06] Jordan: Scoring approach? How do you combine automated metrics and human scores?
[00:03:10] Priya: We recommend a weighted rubric: 50% human acceptability (binary pass/fail on critical items), 30% factuality/hallucination score (human-labeled on golden set), 20% structural/format compliance measured via regex/heuristics and tokenized similarity. Threshold to pass pilot: overall score >= 0.8 and hallucination <= 3%.
[00:03:33] Jordan: Could you show an example of the structural checks?
[00:03:36] Priya: Sure — mandatory sections: HPI, Assessment, Plan. Format checks ensure Plan includes bullet list of action items, meds listed in Medication section, dates not invented (regex check for dates), and no PHI leakage patterns.
[00:03:52] Samir: For throughput, our median encounter is ~1,200 tokens after transcription. We expect 600-800 concurrent users at peak; typical submit rate ~200 reqs/minute.
[00:04:03] Alex: We'll translate that to concurrent model streams. With a typical 2k-context model and batch sizing we expect to need X GPUs — Priya can add numbers.
[00:04:12] Priya: Rough back-of-envelope: 200 reqs/min with 1,200 token avg and target p95 latency of <1s for summary tail is aggressive. For the pilot we'll measure p50/p95 latency with continuous batching enabled; expected cost profile reported. We'll provide a machine-level plan for Redwood Dedicated vs hosted.
[00:04:30] Jordan: We care about latency for clinician UX — under 3s is a hard requirement for interactive flows. Background batch jobs can be longer.
[00:04:36] Priya: Noted — we'll include that in the benchmark.
[00:04:40] Maya: On audit logs: we need immutable event logs for every inference, and the ability to export anonymized transcripts for audits. Does Redwood support that?
[00:04:48] Alex: Yes, request-level logging with trace IDs. For hosted we'll need to configure retention and redaction. We'll send the audit log sample schema.
[00:04:57] Jordan: Walk me through the regression testing plan during the pilot.
[00:05:01] Priya: Two parallel tracks: automated regression — run new model/prompt combos against golden set and flag regressions automatically (delta in score > 5% triggers alert). Human regression — sample N examples weekly for clinician grading. We'll keep a baseline snapshot and produce diffs.
[00:05:18] Samir: For automated hallucination detection — is that rule-based or model-based? We've seen both with varying false positive rates.
[00:05:24] Priya: We'll use hybrid: rule-based detectors for obvious patterns (invented meds/dates) and an ML-based entailment check for more subtle contradictions. We'll tune thresholds with your labels.
[00:05:36] Jordan: Who will annotate the golden set? Vara clinicians or Redwood annotators?
[00:05:41] Alex: We usually co-annotate. Proposal: Vara provides 100 candidate golden examples; Redwood provides an annotation guide and does the initial pass; then 10 Vara clinicians do final accept/reject sampling.
[00:05:54] Maya: For privacy we need the annotation process to happen in your secure environment or via our VPC.
[00:06:00] Alex: We can run annotations inside your VPC if you prefer; otherwise we use webhook redaction and secure S3 with KMS. We'll add options in the SOW.
[00:06:11] Jordan: Regarding timeline — what's realistic for a 4-week pilot start to finish?
[00:06:15] Priya: Week 0 (prep): share sample data, align golden set and rubric. Week 1: dry-run benchmarks and prompt iteration. Week 2: run full bench on 500 samples, human annotation start. Week 3: regression runs and tuning. Week 4: final eval + pass/fail review and economics summary.
[00:06:35] Samir: If we sign by next Monday, can you hit those dates?
[00:06:39] Alex: Yes, assuming data arrives within 48 hours.
[00:06:42] Jordan: Cost — ballpark for pilot?
[00:06:45] Alex: Pilot cost depends on model variants and retention options. Roughly $6k–$12k for a 4-week pilot including engineering time and up to 50k tokens/day testing across variants. We'll send firm quote in SOW.
[00:06:58] Maya: Any known limitations with medical terminologies — e.g., SNOMED/ICD code mapping?
[00:07:03] Priya: Out-of-the-box models won't map perfectly to ICD; we suggest a post-processing step with a mapping table and a small ruleset. If you want higher fidelity mapping, that's a separate mapping microservice or an ML classifier in a follow-up.
[00:07:18] Samir: For evaluation metrics, you mentioned ROUGE-ish. Could we include BERTScore or clinicalBERT similarity?
[00:07:24] Priya: Absolutely — we can include embedding-based similarity (clinical embedding) and custom task-specific heuristics. We'll add those to the benchmark sheet.
[00:07:33] Jordan: On the golden prompts, we'll likely need 6-8 variants to cover different clinician styles.
[00:07:38] Priya: Yep — we'll draft those and put them in the shared sheet for you to iterate.
[00:07:43] Alex: Quick note — we recommend keeping an immutable snapshot of each model/prompt combo during the pilot so the regression diffs are valid.
[00:07:51] Samir: For the technical deep-dive later, Priya, can you prepare latency profiles per model variant and batch config?
[00:07:57] Priya: Will do. I'll also include expected token/sec and memory profiles.
[00:08:03] Jordan: Any red flags we should be aware of?
[00:08:05] Priya: Potential red flags: high hallucination on rare entity mentions, tokens blowup with very long transcripts, and edge-case deadlines for regulatory exports. We'll monitor and escalate.
[00:08:16] Maya: Security question — do you support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for hosted?
[00:08:20] Alex: Yes, we support KMS integrations and HSM options on Private deployments. We'll include config options in the security doc.
[00:08:28] Jordan: Alright, let's talk specifics of the golden set. We'll identify 120 high-risk examples covering meds, allergies, and orders.
[00:08:36] Samir: We'll label each with expected fields and acceptability criteria.
[00:08:40] Priya: Great — the annotation guide will list labels: hallucination flag, factual_error_type, structure_pass, clinician_accept. We'll calibrate the labels with example disagreements to keep consistency.
[00:08:55] Jordan: For regression automation — what's your alerting cadence?
[00:08:59] Priya: We run nightly diffs during pilot; any model that drops >5% in composite score triggers a PagerDuty alert to assigned engineers.
[00:09:06] Alex: Also adding an executive summary weekly for stakeholders.
[00:09:11] Jordan: That helps. On deliverables — can Redwood produce a short runbook for triaging hallucinations?
[00:09:17] Priya: Yes — we'll include remediation steps, rollback instructions, and fallback policies (e.g., revert to earlier model or degrade to extractive summary).
[00:09:27] Jordan: Perfect. Any open items we didn't cover?
[00:09:30] Maya: Need concrete retention numbers for logs and the sample export protocol.
[00:09:34] Alex: We'll include both options in SOW: 30-day hosted retention or customer-defined retention on VPC.
[00:09:40] Samir: One more: we'll want token-level cost estimates per 1k tokens across candidate models.
[00:09:45] Priya: We'll attach a cost matrix in the quote.
[00:09:49] Alex: Ok let's recap — agreed action items: Redwood sends SOW/pricing + benchmark harness; Vara shares 500 de-id notes and 120 golden candidates; annotation guide and security doc to be circulated. Follow-up meeting to review initial benchmarks week of July 27.
[00:10:05] Jordan: Sounds good to me. Thanks all.
[00:10:07] Alex: Thanks, we'll send notes and link to bench sheet.
[00:10:10] [--- brief pause, off-topic chat about summer plans ~2m ---]
[00:12:20] [00:12:20] Jordan: Back on — Samir, you'll coordinate data delivery?
[00:12:24] Samir: Yep, will put files in the secure upload by end of day Monday.
[00:12:30] [00:12:30] Maya: I'll confirm legal redaction checklist.
[00:12:34] Alex: Great. End recap: pilot start target Mon July 20, 2026 if SOW signed and data ingested.
[00:12:44] Jordan: Endorsed.
[00:12:46] [Wrap-up chatter and goodbyes]
[00:51:30] Meeting end.

Transcript notes: occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., "Redwood Dedicate" instead of "Redwood Dedicated"), filler words, and speaker overlap present. The call included concrete commitments and the plan for a 4-week pilot with explicit acceptance gates and a mixed automated/human evaluation approach.
